concepts.title: Clinical Nutrition and Medical Nutrition Therapy
concepts.definition: The branch of nutrition that plans food intake for people during sickness -- now widely called Medical Nutrition Therapy -- connecting what a patient eats with immunity, healing and disease control.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- nutrition status plus illness decides recovery and complications
concepts.key_idea: Adequate nourishment defends the body against infection and speeds recovery, while poor nourishment deepens existing disease.

solution_steps.action: define the field: nutrition management of patients with established disease
solution_steps.explain: it sits between food science and medicine

solution_steps.action: link status to outcome: weak intakes weaken immune defence, wound healing, organ function
solution_steps.explain: support before and after illness shapes prognosis

concepts.title: Role and Functions of the Dietitian
concepts.definition: A dietitian or medical nutrition therapist turns the doctor's diagnosis into a diet prescription, assesses each patient, supervises hospital food service and counsels the patient so the plan is actually followed.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- diagnosis plus assessment gives the nutrition care plan
concepts.key_idea: The dietitian is the nutrition member of the medical team: the physician treats the disease, the dietitian manages the diet.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe102.txt, Basic Concepts and dietitian responsibilities (approx lines 201-352)

solution_steps.action: trace the care sequence: assess status, diagnose the nutrition problem, plan and prioritise intervention, monitor and evaluate

concepts.title: Nutritional Assessment
concepts.definition: The evidence gathering stage that combines health, diet, medication and personal histories with anthropometric measurements and laboratory values to expose current deficiencies and future risks.
concepts.formula: assessment = history plus body measurements plus laboratory readings, all interpreted together
concepts.key_idea: No sound diet plan can precede a measured picture of the patient's status and needs.

solution_steps.action: collect the histories: health, diet, personal, medication
solution_steps.explain: these reveal habits, allergies and drug nutrient clashes

solution_steps.action: add measurements and laboratory data, then interpret
solution_steps.explain: the physician's diagnosis ties the findings together and flags deficiencies

concepts.title: Objectives of Diet Therapy
concepts.definition: Planning a therapeutic diet aims to speed recovery, reshape the usual diet to keep the disease in check, fix deficiencies, guard against short and long term complications, and teach the patient to adhere to the plan.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- recovery plus control plus correction plus prevention plus adherence
concepts.key_idea: A plan respects the patient's food habits, culture, occupation and pocket, or it simply will not be followed.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe102.txt, objectives of diet therapy (approx lines 222-240)

solution_steps.action: list the five objectives in order

solution_steps.explain: these decide whether the plan survives contact with the patient

concepts.title: Types of Diets and Dietary Modification
concepts.definition: A regular diet covers all food groups for a healthy person; modified diets adjust consistency, energy, nutrient levels, meal spacing or the feeding route to answer a patient's medical needs.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- each modification serves one medical purpose
concepts.key_idea: Protein goes up after surgery and down in kidney failure; sodium and fluid may be capped; oxalate rich foods like spinach may be restricted.

solution_steps.action: define the regular diet and its hospital version
solution_steps.explain: hospitals trim fried fatty items, sweets and heavy spices even from normal diets

solution_steps.action: enumerate the four modification levers: consistency, energy, nutrient amounts, meal pattern or route
solution_steps.explain: one or more levers are pulled to fit the diagnosis

concepts.title: Consistency Changes: Liquid and Soft Diets
concepts.definition: Diets are thinned or softened to match chewing and swallowing ability: full fluid and clear liquid regimens after surgery or for swallowing trouble, soft and mechanical soft regimens for weak digestion or denture and teething difficulties.
concepts.formula: qualitative ladder -- clear liquid to full fluid to soft to mechanical soft to regular
concepts.key_idea: Clear liquids follow an operation but cannot meet full nutrient needs for long; fibreless fluids absorb easily.
question_patterns: differentiate between a clear liquid diet and a full fluid diet

solution_steps.action: order the consistency levels and their users
solution_steps.explain: post surgery cases start on clear soups and pulp free juices; chewing problems call for khichdi style soft meals or mashed purees

solution_steps.action: note the purpose of each level
solution_steps.explain: rest to the digestive tract, easy absorption, freedom from harsh fibre and spice

worked_examples.q: Which regimen follows immediately after an operation: clear liquid or regular?

concepts.title: Feeding Routes: Oral, Tube and Intravenous
concepts.definition: Feeding by mouth is the first choice; when chewing or swallowing fails, complete liquid feeds travel down a tube passed through the nose into the stomach, and when the gut cannot work, prepared solutions drip into a vein.
concepts.formula: route choice -- mouth first, tube next, vein last
concepts.key_idea: Tube feeding beats intravenous feeding whenever the gastrointestinal tract can still digest and absorb.
question_patterns: name the routes used to feed a patient who cannot swallow

solution_steps.action: rank the routes and their conditions
solution_steps.explain: mouth for the able, nose to stomach tube for the blocked or unconscious, vein for a non working gut

solution_steps.action: justify the preference order
solution_steps.explain: a functional gut digests and absorbs complete feeds better than any drip

worked_examples.q: Which feeding route is the first choice: oral or intravenous?

concepts.title: Diet, Lifestyle and Chronic Disease Prevention
concepts.definition: Urban plates have drifted towards more fat, refined sugar and salt with less fibre, a shift that feeds obesity, diabetes, hypertension, colon cancer and heart trouble, so early diet counselling can push back the age of onset.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- refined plus high fat plus high salt diets raise chronic disease risk
concepts.key_idea: Convenience foods high in sodium and low in potassium rich fruits and vegetables, with little activity and much stress, drive blood pressure up.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe102.txt, Prevention of Chronic Diseases and exercise box studies (approx lines 417-471)

solution_steps.action: map the dietary drift: more fat, sugar, salt and animal protein, less fibre and micronutrients
solution_steps.explain: refined processed foods carry additives and shed beneficial constituents

solution_steps.action: connect drift to disease: obesity, colon cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, hypertension
solution_steps.explain: less activity and more stress multiply the effect

solution_steps.action: state the preventive role of the nutritionist
solution_steps.explain: counselling in schools, colleges and clinics corrects choices before disease sets in

concepts.title: Study Risk Arithmetic
concepts.section: Exercise box: diet and disease studies
concepts.definition: A diet disease study that quotes a percentage fall in risk lets you compute the danger still left: take the stated percent of the baseline risk away from the baseline.
concepts.key_idea: A 52 percent fall in risk leaves 48 percent of the original risk in play.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe102.txt, exercise box clinical studies (approx lines 459-471)
question_patterns: a study links weekly fish meals to a 52 percent drop in sudden death risk; if the baseline risk is 50 per 1000 men, what risk remains

a dietary claim promises a 25 percent reduction from a baseline risk of 80; find the new risk level
work out the risk left once the stated percentage reduction is applied to the initial level

solution_steps.action: size the reduction
solution_steps.explain: multiply the baseline by the percentage cut and divide by one hundred

solution_steps.action: subtract the cut from the baseline
solution_steps.explain: whatever remains is the risk still carried after the dietary change

worked_examples.q: A 52 percent fall in risk leaves what percent of the original risk?

concepts.title: Post-Harvest Wastage Share
concepts.definition: A fixed fraction of harvested fruits, vegetables and milk spoils before processing; the tonnage lost is that fraction applied to the whole harvest, which is exactly why food processing is urged upon the country.
concepts.key_idea: Between a fifth and a third of produce perishes, so preservation and processing convert losses into products and jobs.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe102.txt, unit introduction on produce wastage (approx lines 43-59)
question_patterns: about one fifth of a 5000 tonne fruit harvest spoils before processing; compute the tonnage wasted

solution_steps.action: apply the spoilage fraction to the harvest
solution_steps.explain: multiply the total produce by the wasted share to get the loss
